sources.title: RFC 2119 and RFC 8174: requirement-keyword meanings
sources.author: Scott Bradner; Barry Leiba
sources.accessScope: Both documents read for BCP 14 keyword semantics, including uppercase qualification.
sources.rights: IETF Trust/BCP 78 terms apply; no boilerplate or source wording bundled.

rules.intent: Preserve facts, numbers, units, negation, conditions, exceptions, uncertainty, quotations, citations, and code at every level.
rules.rationale: Shared project meaning-preservation requirement; style never authorizes factual change.

rules.intent: Define scope, terminology, actors, and assumptions before normative behavior.
rules.rationale: Original operational guidance adapted from the identified source scope.

rules.intent: Preserve obligation strength and use BCP 14 uppercase keywords only with an explicit declaration of their meaning.
rules.rationale: Original operational guidance adapted from the identified source scope.
exceptions: Normative requirements can use ordinary prose; do not introduce keywords or stronger obligations without intent.

rules.intent: Use suitable abstract, introduction, technical sections, security considerations, and IANA applicability statements without inventing facts or registrations.
rules.rationale: Original operational guidance adapted from the identified source scope.
exceptions: For an internal proposal, explain when IANA is not applicable; do not pretend an external allocation exists.

rules.intent: Distinguish documents needed to implement the specification from contextual or explanatory references.
rules.rationale: Original operational guidance adapted from the identified source scope.
exceptions: A URL alone does not prove the source is authoritative or normative.
